instructions: Ambiguity hunt. Choose the answer labels, then argue the strongest case for one wrong option in case {label, text}. Set flag to one sentence when that case is defensible or a constraint is missing, else null.

items.stem: A company runs an API on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. The group is attached to a target group of an Application Load Balancer and keeps its default health check settings. After some days of running, a memory leak makes the API on some instances return HTTP 503 errors. The target group marks these instances as unhealthy, but they stay in the group, and the other instances become overloaded. The company must ensure that such instances are replaced automatically. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Configure the target group to terminate each instance that fails its health checks, so that the Auto Scaling group launches a new instance in its place.

options.label: B
options.text: Turn on Elastic Load Balancing health checks for the Auto Scaling group, so that the group also acts on the health that the load balancer reports.

options.label: C
options.text: Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm on the unhealthy host count of the target group that invokes an AWS Lambda function to mark each failing instance unhealthy.

options.label: D
options.text: Turn on Amazon EBS health checks for the Auto Scaling group, so that the group also replaces each instance whose API returns HTTP 503 errors.

items.stem: A company created an Auto Scaling group with the AWS CLI and later turned on Elastic Load Balancing health checks for it. The group runs a web application behind an Application Load Balancer. The application needs about 4 minutes after launch before it answers the target group health checks. Now each new instance is terminated and replaced again and again, so the group does not reach its desired capacity. Instances whose application fails later must still be replaced. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Set the health check grace period of the group to a value that is longer than the time that the application needs to start.

options.label: B
options.text: Add a launch lifecycle hook, and change the user data script so that it completes the lifecycle action when the application answers requests.

options.label: C
options.text: Change the health check type of the group back to Amazon EC2 status checks only, so that the group ignores the target group results.

options.label: D
options.text: Increase the default cooldown of the group, so that the group waits longer before it replaces an instance that fails its health checks.

items.stem: A company runs a web application on one Amazon EC2 instance. The application keeps its state in memory and cannot run as several copies. During the day the load changes often, and at peaks the CPU utilization of the instance reaches 100%. Users then see slow responses. The company expects the number of users to grow during the next year. The application must handle the growth and the daily peaks with minimal downtime. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.label: A
options.text: Attach a second elastic network interface to the instance, so that the instance can accept twice as many user requests during the peaks.

options.label: B
options.text: Change the instance to a larger instance type with more vCPUs and more memory, and move to a larger type again each time the load grows.

options.label: C
options.text: Turn on detailed monitoring for the instance, so that Amazon CloudWatch publishes the CPU utilization metric every minute instead of every five minutes.

options.label: D
options.text: Run the application in an Auto Scaling group across two Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer, with a target tracking scaling policy on CPU utilization.
